axis_coverage.name: Original obligations and negative constraints
axis_coverage.reason: The final is a complete planning proposal for the five-collection catalogue. It compares staged Europeana aggregation with Omeka publishing, adds DPLA implementation/history, and supplies SKOS/Getty/PROV analogies. It distinguishes supplied statement, license, public-domain assertion/tool and local access policy, retains exact source values/identifiers/scope with change provenance, and handles missing/conflicting values without favorable defaults. Registrar and metadata-lead authority remains exact. Both optional capabilities are retained with technical/owner conditions. The unsafe binary map, blanket permission badge, thumbnail inference, restricted retrieval and unknown-to-public-domain conversion are rejected. Product choice, collection facts and owner approvals are not invented. Every exact plan clause and handoff validation row is dispositioned below; no new implementation or legal determination is demanded.

axis_coverage.reason: Independent governing-source review supports the consequential subjects, operations, versions, defaults, types/domains and exceptions. These include DPLA-specific mapping/rights validation; historical EDM aggregation/WebResource scope; IIIF versioned fields and machine/visible statements; Omeka CSV empty-cell/duplicate-ID semantics, suggestions/label loss, OAI publishing/media default/deletion limit, public reads/authenticated writes and conditional one-way importer overwrite exceptions. The final correctly states resource-wide RDF replacement for PATCH. Documentation/version evidence is distinct from runtime behavior. Official vocabulary context supports CNE/UND despite canonical-page retrieval failures. Minor locator limits and living-documentation deployment pinning remain; no remaining material wrong source condition or unsupported consequential choice was found. The independent evidence matrix below records each source separately, rather than relying on agreement or hashes.

Draft/final add Omeka publishing, CSV update hazards, optional OAI/API output, suggestion/label-loss risks and a conditional Item Importer path. These lead to concrete record/provenance and per-collection update proposals, not a product list or vacuous caution. History is bounded rather than projected onto the five unidentified museums. Exhaustive product selection or deployment is not required. Minor depth/opportunity limits are the omitted explicit dual/version-negotiated migration option and leaving CSV Undo scope as a manual tension despite a public released-code answer. Neither yields a wrong product choice or removal of authorized scope.

axis_coverage.reason: The final distinguishes desk research and reveal control from product operation. Checks discriminate empty/omitted fields, duplicates, multi-valued rights, versioned visible text/URI semantics, full/delta/partial/failed runs, explicit delete versus omission, rejected deletes/backfill, privacy and source-attributed outputs for each collection. Oracles must use supplied sanitized values, owner-approved scopes/maps, pinned profiles, expected ID/count reconciliation and actual clients—not legal truth, source counts, hashes, task status or one provider's example.
